utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Usher -- yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I would just like to inform you that my client is not feeling well today. He definitely wants to be present at the cross-examination. We do not know how long it will take. He believes that he can make it through the cross-examination, but after I finish my cross-examination, perhaps if he does not feel better, he would like to be excused. This is all I wanted to bring up this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, your request is granted. And with your client's absence, we'll continue to do the cross-examination. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client is hoping to be able to attend the entire cross-examination of this witness, and I will give you an update after that on his health. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness after you pull down -- pulling down the blinds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So-so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just have the ELMO lowered, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we can see each other. Good morning. Let me introduce myself. I am the attorney for Mladen Naletilic, and I will ask you some questions. I will ask you, as I asked of every witness, to please pause between questions and answer for the benefit of the interpreters who are involved in a difficult task. And I would also like you to listen carefully to what I ask and please try to make your answers as concise as possible. I'm going to especially focus on what you personally have seen or heard. Thank you for your cooperation, and I would like to move to my questions now. Can you confirm for me that the evidence that you gave yesterday and the day before yesterday and the statement that you gave to the Prosecution -- Prosecution in this case, it would seem that you personally never saw Tuta in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also confirm for me - and again it would follow from your answer - that you never saw Tuta and Baja together in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you also confirm to me on the basis of what you just said that you were never in a position to hear any conversation, let alone any orders that Tuta may have given to Baja in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "in Mostar," does that include Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I really am referring to Mostar. Siroki Brijeg is about 30 kilometres away from Mostar. This is why I limited myself exclusively to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when I say "Baja," I refer to Mr. Milicivic. We both agree that we refer to Baja as Mr. Milicivic.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mario Milicivic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mario Milicivic. So everything that you testified about on the basis of all that you have said, it would not follow that what you have heard from him could or could not have been that way. You only could believe in what he was saying; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, regarding the ATG Benko Penavic, was it not formed out of the 2nd Battalion, and did it not consist exclusively from the men from the 2nd Battalion whose commander was first Tihomir Misic called Tiho and later on his father, Dedo Misic? In other words, this man from the ATG that you called Benko Penavic, were these men not exclusively the men from the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But they were selected men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Do you know - because at that time you were 17 years old - did you know what brigade was the 2nd Battalion part of?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that is a superfluous question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may be superfluous, but do you know at all the command structure in the city of Mostar? This is why I asked you the question. But I don't want to go into any explanations now. My question is: Was this battalion part of some brigade or a part of the defence forces. Over perhaps to make it easier for you, who is the commander of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was talking about Dr. Naletilic, not 2nd Battalion of the brigade. I was referring directly to ATG Benko Penavic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is fine, sir. I am just trying to help the Trial Chamber and all of us to clarify certain things in Mostar. Today we're not going to talk only about the ATG Benko Penavic. And perhaps I should clarify this question for you. Benko Penavic did not come out of nowhere. I want to just lay out the history of this unit a little bit. But first of all, I want to know, because you were 17 at that time, in other words you were quite young at that time, do you know at all how this military structure, this hierarchy in Mostar looked like? If you know, you know. If not, you don't.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: See, you said that I was 17. I was old enough to fight. So we should not take age in any particular way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with you, sir, completely. But if you would like to help me and the Trial Chamber, with all due respect to everything you have said so far. I'm going to ask you a specific question: Do you know who was the commander of the defence of the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically in 1993.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. It was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are -- People say this: "He was the one who was gathering cloths and dispersing cloths." You claim that Mr. Naletilic was the Commander of defence of the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm not saying that he was the commander of defence, but he had everything under his control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he had full control. In other words, he had command control over all battalions, all brigades in the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be able to say whether he had control over all the battalions, but for the most part of the defence forces of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you took part in the war in 1992 and 1993 as a member of the HVO. Did you hear that there was a command of the city -- the military commander of the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that there were brigade commanders, that there was the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that there was the main headquarters of the HVO which was also in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that there were operative zones?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that the city of Mostar was -- the city of Mostar was part of the south-east Herzegovina operative zone?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I told you at the beginning to please limit yourself to saying what you personally know, especially what you saw and heard personally, rather than hearsay. My learned friend asked you a lot about those kinds of things. I'm going to ask you about what you personally saw or heard. As a regular soldier and a member of the 2nd Battalion, you -- when you were in the 2nd Battalion, you did not know who was your superior to your battalion. Listen, it's not funny. If you know, you know. But if you don't know, you don't know. I'm -- I'm trying to test your knowledge, and I would like your answers. I would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to try to answer all the questions that I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also you should understand that the period between the time when I left Mostar and now is ten years and that the structures and the activities that took place in that city is something that is not also easy to remember. But what I know is from whom I was receiving orders and if there were any things that were not clear, with whom it was that they needed to be cleared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, and I thank you for this question. But in essence, you don't know the truth. You could believe what people told you or not. I think that we have agreed on that.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have put it this way: If Tuta had put Baja to lead this Benko Penavic, he was the person to be trusted, to be believed. And if that man said that things were in such and such a way, I was supposed to believe it and follow it and do those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me the fact that Tuta had appointed Baja is only your guess. You don't know personally that he did so.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness, the front line on the Bulevar, how many units were there?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you ask me more specific questions, please, because Bulevar was a fairly long stretch. If you can ask me from where to where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is clear where the line stretched from, Santiceva to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say this: From the old cinema to the health centre, that was the 4th Battalion, and Benko Penavic, and next to it was Stela. I did not go to the other sectors of the front line so, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the position held by the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were around Podhum. It's either Podhum or Zahum, to the ladies' park, and then it was ATG Benko Penavic, and then next to it was ATG Skrobo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of one of the commanders of the 4th Battalion nicknamed Gaga?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can we go into the private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session. Wait, wait, wait. Yes, now we are in the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you those things personally, personally to you Witness?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did he do it? By telephone? In a letter? Leaving a message?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Face to face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness, perhaps we're talking at cross-purposes. A while ago you said that Baja at times left on his own business and did not report to you. So when he told you about this, it couldn't be face to face for you, because you're on the line and he goes somewhere. So my question is: How did he do that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't spend six months on the line day in, day out. We did have some days off when we were not on the front line, when we did nothing, when we were merely on the alert.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally ever visit the headquarters of the defence of the city of Mostar in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask Your Honours, with your leave, that the witness be shown Prosecution's Exhibit P521. Will you please be so kind and look at the first page first. Witness ...

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read the first page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. First we'll look at it together, and then I'll tell you what to read.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So whilst Their Honours are looking for the document, will you please tell me what do you see in the upper left corner of the first page.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 1st Battalion of the Mostar military police. And then we have the reference number, the date. Isn't it the 15th of July 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document please be placed on the ELMO, because the interpreters were not given the document.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then it says the central sector, and after that you have in capital letters "report."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document please be placed on the ELMO, because the interpreters were not given a copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And last passage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, the interpreters say that they did not have the document. Could it be put on the ELMO so that to help the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, it can be done. Yes, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At least the English version of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: What page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, last passage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found it, Witness? Let me just see if it -- no, no, no. One passage below this one. The passage below this one. The paragraph below this one. The next paragraph. The next passage. That's fine. That's fine. So do you see, Witness, what it says here? So Aleksic's house - Zahum front line. So this is the front line from the intersection by the health centre to the church, that is, Zahum. Is that right? And then it says nicely here: "Members of the 4th Battalion of the third HVO brigade are holding the position. And then the enemy continued their customary provocations with sniper fire and so on and so forth." And then the report for that particular day. And that was - let me repeat it once again - it was the 15th of July, 1993. Do you recall that day, the 15th of July? Were you there?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd rather not be asked about the dates. You're saying 15th of July? Can I say something? If you want me to talk about the 15th of July --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this -- this is a report on the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of July, I was not on the front line, because it was then that I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, look at the last sentence in this report. One of our soldiers was likely wounded in the leg. That was you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was wounded next to Livo's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And you see this is a collective report. You can have a look at it. So we have the "glass bank," the old secondary school house line, Aleksica house front line, Zahum. See, somebody was writing a joint report about the developments, which means that somebody coordinated the front line as a whole, issued orders, and received reports. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose it is highly likely. Whether that is so or not, I wouldn't go into it. These are the documents that I was handed over by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that the 4th Battalion was an integral part of the 3rd HVO Brigade? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that every brigade had its own ATGs?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I wouldn't agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can agree with me and you don't have to agree with me. My question was whether you are -- you were aware that brigades as large units incorporated ATGs or special purpose units, or whatever they were called, but that every brigade had units of that kind.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aware of special purpose units, but I'm not aware that ATG units -- that ATGs were parts of brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can you tell apart ATG units and special purpose units? Isn't it one and the same with only names that are different?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the 4th Battalion had also a special purpose unit. Later on, there was also an anti-terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what your army card said when, according to your testimony, you were a member of the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have this document, and I hope you will believe me. And it says "the soldier JPN." Does not -- that JPN, is not that the acronym for the special purpose unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Poriouvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Well, show the document. He's talking about some document without showing it to the witness and to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour. Yes, I have to think about everything, then I forget something. This is part -- this is one of the documents that I received yesterday and why we -- why this cross-examination moves -- moved to today. And this copy fortunately is quite clear. Some other copies -- and I will later on ask my learned friends to help me, both with originals and English translations, because I think that these documents are highly relevant and of great importance. I have one copy because I was given only one copy, and I had no time to -- I mean, but the Chamber received these documents from the Prosecutor yesterday. These documents were attached to this statement that this witness gave to the OTP. So usher, can you please show this document to the witness ask then give it back to me, because this is the only copy that I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen it, your army card?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your card?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that you in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this JP -- does this acronym mean that you were a soldier and that the JPN means "special purpose unit"?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as early as 1992, you were already a member of the special purpose unit.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was a part of the 4th Battalion, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, the gentleman who is mentioned today, Mario Milicivic, that 1992 was also foot soldier like you, wasn't he, and he was also a member of the special purpose unit, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was towards the end, perhaps towards the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your Commander was Mr. Vinko Martinovic, called Vina; right?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, we had a number of commanders. One of them was Vinko Martinovic, Vina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another Commander was a man whose nickname was Benito, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, this gentleman whose nickname is Benito, would you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it that same Benito about whom you said that he mined the Balinovac and destroyed it? Is that the same Benito?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now in 1993 from the special purpose unit, as a matter of fact you remained a special purpose unit except that now you are called the anti-terrorist group, because it's the same men, Baja Milicivic, Benito, and all those men whom you mentioned yesterday and who are in the transcript. I don't have to repeat them. It's all those same men, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm saying that this special purpose unit that we've just been talking about. So you, Baja Milicivic, Benito, all members of this special purpose unit, except that it is now called the anti-terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but under a different commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just clarify something that is not quite clear in the transcript. Since you speak English, it will be easier for you. It says under a different commander. One commander or a different command? What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A while ago you were answering me question, and you said, "Yes, but under a different command." Was that your answer?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that you were under a different command because that is what Baja Milicivic had told you.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is all that you know about it. All that you know comes from Baja Milicivic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Baja Milicivic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you showed your certificate during the testimony for the Prosecution. Why are you on the record? Why are you listed here as a member of the 1st Light Assault Brigade of the military police?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday my learned friend showed you this certificate. I can give it to you today again.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you then, please. I'd like to see every document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, can you please help me. Just don't put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And don't read out your name, please, of course. And so you see the last sentence in this certificate reads: "Whenever something is not clear, contact the unit, Benko Penavic ATG, and the military police, the 1st Light Assault, which has this soldier on its payroll, in its record." And this is P621.1. So you were recorded as a member of the 1st Light Assault. You were on their list.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was listed with the Benko Penavic ATG and the 1st Light Assault. And it says clearly here where this soldier is registered, so in case if necessary this soldier could be contacted either through Benko Penavic or through the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It transpires, then, that you were a member of two different units.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I was in the records of the military police or the ATG Benko Penavic, it does not mean that I am a member of two different units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you are the one who can answer that. I asked you?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've just answered. It does not mean that -- how did they keep their records and whether they kept it well. Was I to be concerned about it? What I had to worry about was how to get out of it all alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait, now. Witness you volunteered. Your father signed your assent. But you wanted to join HVO units. And since you were underage, even your father had to sign the consent form on your behalf. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well then, since you voluntarily joined these unit, you must have been aware that you could also lose your life in a war. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I must object. It's a speculation. My learned colleague told -- just told that he joined some units. The witness say that is he was a member of one unit. He has never told that he was a member of some units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you have to rephrase your question to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when I say that he joined, I believe that we're all following this trial. We have not forgotten it overnight. And especially since I cross-examined him today. He was a member of several units. In 1992 he joined a unit which still did not have its name. I remember his testimony. And only later on it became the 4th Battalion. Today we learned that within the 4th Battalion, he was a member of the Special Purpose Unit. And after that, that there was the ATG. And I think that these are different units. So I think my questions are quite proper. It is no speculation. These are all hard facts. But I can rephrase my question. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ask your question in the proper sequence so that the witness understands where you are aiming at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For that, I don't know when you have decided to take a break. I don't know if it is now. If this is the moment, when we can continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll proceed until 10.15, or quarter past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in 1992, was there any organisation of the defence, or did you self-organise in the defence against the Serb aggression. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that people bought their own weapons or they received it from either the SDA or the HDZ parties?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you organise yourselves by neighbourhoods, by street, and did you sort of find among yourselves your leaders by seniority or some other principle, and only later in late 1992 or 1993 the organisation became more serious, to say?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this way: When was the HVO established?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. You are confronting me with some dates that I cannot answer to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. When did you start organising yourselves as more or less an army out of these self-organised units?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were organised as military organisations from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But a moment ago you said about -- something about the organisation itself. That it's self-organisation.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I am going too fast. I'm now waiting -- looking at the monitor. It has -- I'm waiting for the transcript to stop. So I apologise. But on the other hand, we can concentrate better, we can give better questions and answers to each other. But let's move on. This HVO was formed and then within this HVO, this 4th Battalion was established. I'm now talking in general terms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is now your neighbourhood, your street, and that is part of the 4th Battalion area.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you joined this 4th Battalion when you became a soldier and when you joined.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a weapon from before, and you were together with the Croats in this unit.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when you were in that 4th Battalion - and now we're moving to early 1993 - were ever -- were you ever approached by the ABiH members, and did they say that you should stay with the HVO units because they needed you there for as long as possible?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that this is what they were saying to every -- to all other Muslims who were in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, now the exchange is flowing very well. So they told you to stay in those units until you are needed by the ABiH, and after that you would receive new assignments. Was that how it was approximately?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll take it slowly. Let's limit ourselves to you personally. The 4th Battalion, how many were you? How many Muslims were there in the 4th Battalion approximately?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you few? Were you more than few? Were you a lot?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were few.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then at some point, other Muslims who are members of the ABiH come to you, and what do they say? You tell me.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their representatives of the ABiH came, and they said that there were rumours about a conflict between the Muslims and the Croats but that we -- those of us who were Muslims and who were with the HVO should stay where we are because we were needed there, because there will be no conflict between the HVO and the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you visited for the last time, if you recall, of course?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that they visited us -- they had visited us once, but I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did the ABiH arrest any HVO soldiers? For instance, did they ever arrest any of your fellow soldiers from the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, once at the front line when a conflict broke out between the Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that not sometime before the conflict, that is, sometime in March or April?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You recently gave your statement to the OTP, and you said that it was before the 8th of May. You said that a whole platoon was arrested when they were going to the front lines.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was at the very start of the war between the Muslims and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't know that there was a war at that time.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the 8th of May. I don't know. And after the 8th of May, I also don't know whether that was a war. It is something that history is going to decide and this Trial Chamber. So was it before the 8th of May?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of their being arrested -- having been arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: . I'm sorry. I'm just looking -- I'm trying to find out that place in the statement. In order not to waste time, even though I did mark things, maybe I'll take it up during the break. No, I found it now. I'm sorry. Yes. Yes. My apologies. I will give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Poriouvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... witness statement before him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- my apologies. I thank you for reminding me so promptly, my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "You see, until the 8th of May, 1993, I was doing nothing else but going from time to time to the front lines against the Serbs. The last time I was up there was on either the 2nd or 3rd of May. The platoon that had replaced mine was arrested by the Muslim Armjia at the front line. It is absolutely clear that they were arrested at the front line facing the Serbs, and it was quite clear that it was before the 8th of May." These are your words. Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. I did not say it was before the 8th of May, because you went from 7 to 14 days. So if you -- if you look at the 2nd or 3rd, it would be going to 9th or past 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 11 October 2001, that is, two months ago, you signed this statement and adopted it as your own.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not say that.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say it, but not in the words which you used to explain it, sir. You're looking for proof that the army had arrested these men before the 8th. I did not write that. I said that we were replaced, that we had rotated on the 2nd or the 3rd. I did not say when the arrests took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not trying to polemicise with you, Witness. That is not my intention. I simply read what is written here and whether you had stated that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But after my statement you had an explanation. You concluded that the army had arrested the people before the 8th of May. And that is what I don't agree with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could the usher bring the witness out first, after pulling down the blinds. Mr. Krsnik, would you please furnish us, the judges, with the English version of that statement during the break. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I can do it immediately. I have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll have 30 minutes break, then we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Usher, please wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client is feeling worse. He's feeling worse than before. He's taken this nitroglycerin for three times now, and he would like to be excused. Of course I'm going to go on without his presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, he could be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let us finish off the -- this line of questioning that we had started before the break. Let me put it simply. Do you know whether this platoon of the 4th Battalion was arrested before the 8th of May or not? If you know.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move on. Witness, I'm going to ask the usher -- I'm going to show you a picture. We'll go back to the Bulevar to try to clear up some additional things. I'm going to ask Madam Registrar for that exhibit. Witness, will you please take the pointer. Witness, this exhibit, 14.5, was shown to you yesterday, if I am not mistaken. We mentioned these Aleksica houses here. I was referring to these demolished buildings across from the health centre. Now, was that your position? Or please just show me your position, where it was.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, what I was referring to as Aleksica Kuca is exactly the area that you just showed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, sorry, there's only one house that he showed, and you referred to "houses." Could you have it clarified, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. And in fact, I was just about to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, again, using your pointer first, will you show -- can we pull back the image so that we see as much of it as possible. Excellent. Perfect. Maybe we went a little bit too wide. All these houses that have been demolished, was that your position?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all the demolished houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you then, please, point to which one.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I doubt that I can show you exactly, because it is overgrown now, so you cannot see everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not referring to the area that was controlled by the ABiH but the one that was under your control. So you were holding the position of only this one house?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several houses there. There was a house behind this one. There was a house here. There was a house behind there. There was a wall there. Another house was the Aleksica house. If you want, I can draw it for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. I am trying to make it as clear as possible for the Trial Chamber. So for the record, there were other houses here which have now disappeared. They were what, destroyed or disappeared?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- they're now overgrown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you can draw a straight line. Don't circle it, but just a straight line of what was your sector of the front line of the ATG Benko Penavic.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You think that I can draw a -- exactly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try it, but it may not be perfect or straight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do the best you can.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a green marker, unfortunately, but I hope we can all see it. Tell me, this is Liska Street, northward direction.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, towards Ronda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. These first houses that are so badly damaged, who held those? Whose line was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see which line you're pointing at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure I am really showing the exact position because it's not easy for me to see this green marker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, do you think it would help if you got a chance to look at the actual mark and then the Trial Chamber got a chance to look, because you see, there's a shadow on the picture and we can't tell whether the green mark is there or not. And this is quite crucial. So maybe if you have a look at it, the rest of the team has a look at it, and then when you finish, if you hand it up to us -- and also your client, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd also like to ask the witness to draw a line, if possible, to somehow close this area in the westward direction, and then we shall see it. Because now we see there are only two lines. But you didn't draw a line on the west side. So on the upper side towards Rondo, towards Rondo, how far up did your line go? And then, Your Honour, we shall get a square more or less or a rhomboid.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I could make a suggestion and perhaps the witness could use a black marker and make his drawings, then it will be visible. Okay. Great.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, now we can see it. Now we can see it well, I hope. Your Honour, can you see it now clearly? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question, Witness, is: So between this new building, this white building, to your line, to the upper line, who held that particular building?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which white building, excuse me? Could you point at it to me, because I'd like to avoid any confusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Witness. So this white building, this first white renovated building across the health centre towards Rondo, this big white building with the red roof, left -- to the left of the health centre. So we have a row of demolished houses, and then this building which was renovated. Now, my question is: Between that building and the line that you drew, who held that area?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody did. That is, that area served only for us to get to the line. That is the way we took to the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now will you please tell me -- yes, it's also difficult for me to say where is west, where is east. So we're looking from down Bulevar towards Carinski Bridge; is that right? And from that line, who manned that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can say that from the intersection up to the church, it was only you and the 4th Battalion, is it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And here, in this square, you yourself decided what you would do, or was the whole line under the same command?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In that particular part, we took our own decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, you could launch an attack whenever you liked?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, come, counsel. It was all organised. Who ever saw anyone launch an attack by himself, on his own, come on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for this answer. That is what I'm trying to get from you slowly and gradually. This answer, of course it's a logical answer because across from you along the whole line is the ABiH army, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Let's keep this picture here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I will now have to ask the registrar to give the usher P590. It is another Prosecution exhibit, and I was given this document by the gentleman from the OTP. It can be placed on the ELMO, because I think that no names are mentioned here. Can we have the first page on the ELMO, of the English version. Very good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please listen to what I'm saying. I will only read the title, that is, "The Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, south-eastern Herzegovina operative zone, Mostar"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, pursuant to the order of the main staff -- the GS means the main staff. Then we get the reference number then the year. [As read] For the better function of command and of control systems in forthcoming offensive -- defensive operations, and with the aim of or in order to prevent the break through the defence line towards the MOS, meaning Muslim defence forces, and the VRS, which is the army of Republika Srpska, in the area of responsibility. Clear the Drezanka River valley and take control of Dreznica through offensive and sabotage operations; cleanse Mostar of MOS forces (the right bank), and in further offensive operations, take control of Mostar and Bijelo Polje and take control of the Bijela/Ravni/Salakovac sector. You know where Salakovac is. Salakovac is a dam on the Neretva on at Rastani. And now we have in capital letters I order. And then it says that, South-east Herzegovina's operative zone is hereby divided into three sectors, sector north, sector Mostar Defence, and sector south. Were you aware of this division in the command chain?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- excuse me. No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what we are interested in is the sector of Mostar Defence. It is 1.2. And it says here -- I believe that is page 2 in English. And then it says: "Mostar Defence sector comprises the two HVO brigades; that is, there were two brigades in Mostar." Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [As Read] The current complement of the Mostar Defence, with one third of the brigade, and then in brackets it says VP, the military police, forces of the Mostar police administration, Mrmak ATG, Benko Penavic ATG, and the Home Guard Regiment so organise and prepare offensive and defensive operations in the zone left, and then it -- the text goes on to indicate points of references, such as Macija Glava TT714, excluding Gornje Vojno, Dobro Dublje, TT1112, and to the right, not including how many, in depth, the village of Polog. The sector commander is Mr. Mijo Jelic, command post, Mostar. Now, first question is: Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, all the brigades mentioned in this document would be under the commander of the Mostar Defence and his commander. Will you now turn to the end of the document. And his commander would be the commander of the operative zone of south-east Herzegovina. And as it says here "Brigadier, Milenko Lasic". Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see this order is then delivered. This is left of the signature. It is sent to -- that is, all those to whom copies are sent are listed here. You will not find anywhere here either the military police or the home guard regiment, nor Mrmak ATG, nor Benko Penavic ATG. It is delivered to the Commander of the Mostar Defence sector. And the Commander of the Mostar Defence sent on the order received from the Main Staff to these addresses here. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. You are talking about things that a foot soldier had no way of knowing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a fair answer. That's why I asked you this question. And you answered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And Mr. Krsnik, what's the time frame of that period? I understand this order was issued, at least according to this document, on the 4th of September, 1993. Is that relevant to the testimony of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is, because under 1.2 of this order, we read about the complement prior to that date. That is, it says "Mostar Defence sector comprises two brigades, the current complement, that is, it was prior to the 3rd of September, and that is why I thought it relevant. Moreover, the witness testified about a relatively long period of time, from May until about October when he left. Isn't it, Witness? Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you will agree with me, Witness, you didn't mention too many days nor do we know when happened what, according to you. That is, you know about events but you do not know exactly when they took place.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But now let us go back to the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to ask the registrar merely to present as clear a picture as possible to Their Honours, 14.3, to give us Exhibit 14.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I ask you Mr. Krsnik - and forgive me for interrupting so often - is the point of your cross-examination to establish that this witness was not in the ATG Benko Penavic? What are you actually trying to establish? It's not clear to me why it's so important to say that somebody says that the area of responsibility for the 4th Battalion is in this corner, and you're saying he says the other. What is the aim of this cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should be very happy to do so, Your Honour. And thank you very much for you question. The Defence holds that this was all the 4th Battalion because we already have the testimony about this, and that thought this anti-terrorist group or the elite unit or the anti-terror group, or what other names were used to designate those groups, that they were all part of the brigade, rather, a battalion, in the area of responsibility which was called Mostar Defence in south-eastern Herzegovina. I believe this is very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... your position is that the ATG Benko Penavic was part of the 4th Battalion, part and parcel. So the commander of the 4th Battalion would be this witness's commander. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is right. That is part of the second brigade. That is part of the defence of the city of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Let's not go that far. Just in this particular situation, you are saying that Benko Penavic was part and parcel of the 4th Battalion and not an independent unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not sure this is it, but perhaps we could look at D2/6. There may have been a version of that same photograph 14.5 that was then marked as a Defence exhibit. It might be D2/6 possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll wait a little bit, because we're almost done, and then I'll ask you to show me on this photograph, the one that you're about to be given, again to mark where the 4th Battalion and where the ATG were.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the witness. Can the microphones please be turned on for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please repeat what you just said.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We'll just skip it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The colleagues told me that you are not a painter. So if you --

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you heard it, why are you asking me to repeat it? Please be serious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I had asked you for the transcript, because it was not entered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have in front of me a photograph, and my colleagues have just reminded me that they were leading this evidence, and the house in the photograph marked 14.5 was marked, but we are in open session, but I can hand it over to the usher to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's not really what you said, Mr. Krsnik, is it? It's long distance from what you said. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So the other witness had said that he -- the other witness had allegedly marked a map showing the identical area as being the 4th Battalion area. Now that photograph doesn't show that at all. It shows a house with a circle around it marked number "3," which is outside of the area, at the very back of the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, and I apologise. It's Mr. Poriouvaev's witness, of course, but I'm trying to assist on this particular item with the Chamber's permission. I think you can find some discussion of this at 25 -- for those of you who have the laptop at page 2597/98, of transcript where indeed Mr. Seric was cross-examining that witness concerning these matters and 14.5 was remarked as a Defence Exhibit D2/6. So that page number may assist. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there are several numbers and several markings here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, we can't tell what page it is, Your Honours. My only question is maybe Mr. Scott could tell me what date. I can't -- I have a laptop here, but I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's on the 19th of September. The reference actually to marking the doctor's house is on 25 -- page 2596, approximately line 20. Witness S "Witness S can you point on this photograph at the house of Dr. Aleksic." And it's on 2596 and continuing thereafter on the 19th of September, I believe. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you may proceed. We could look at it during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now finally I'm going to ask you, Witness, to draw another line from the intersection that would be, I guess, due south, towards the customs bridge, the Carinski Bridge, where the 4th Battalion was deployed according to you, so that we see that. I'm going to ask the -- the Madam Registrar for 14.3.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you had already asked me numbers 1 and 2. I put -- oh, I see. This is a different picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is why I was asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Madam Registrar, if it's not a problem. [In English] 14.3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm going to ask you to place that -- no, Mr. Usher is going to handle it. While we are waiting, perhaps you can take the pointer in the other photographs -- the other photograph, you had put number "2" there. So I'll first ask you to use your pointer and show where your area was.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. I am not sure that I'll be able to show very accurately where it was because it's -- it's not a detailed picture, and we could easily be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not the purpose. Do you recognise the intersection from the other photograph? So let me just ask you, then, to show with the pointer where you were and just extend the line to where you think the 4th Battalion was.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. This is where you were.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates] From where we were, all way down to whom was the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll all note it for the record. According to you, the 4th Battalion continued directly from your line to that hill which, as we know, is called Hum.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you -- I don't know what your purpose is. You were talking about the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the Benko Penavic ATG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please hear me out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking the questions.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will not get upset. You will see in the certificate that Mario Milicivic signed that I was a member of the ATG from such and such a date to such and such a date. And it -- and so I don't know why you are pressing me with the questions regarding the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I really do not want to press you. I know that it's not easy to give evidence for as long as you have been giving it. I am doing my job, and I'm trying to clear up certain things. And this certificate, it says that you are a member of the Light Assault Unit of the military police.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the transcript, in case another Court is reading that transcript. I cannot let that pass a second time. Unless the interpretation in English is totally different from what it is in Serbo-Croat, what it says is that this witness is a member of the Benko Penavic Convicts Battalion and that any inquiry in relation to him is to be addressed either to the ATG unit or to the military police. It doesn't say that he's a soldier with the military police. It just says where this soldier is officially registered. It doesn't mean he's a member of the police. That's the interpretation that I take from it, and I think that the -- the record should be clarified, just in case this evidence is considered by another Court. I think I might have interrupted Mr. Poriouvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You did my job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I didn't mean to do that. I was trying to do our job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I owe you an answer. One of the major problems in this trial is the language and meanings which are -- which is very hard to do, even to our very good interpreters. If it is -- if something is registered -- if somebody is registered with a college, let's say, does that mean that the person is actually going to that college? He can be registered somewhere, but it doesn't mean that he is actually going to classes. So this is the meaning of the -- of being registered in the Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Poriouvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I must object. What is the aim of your statement now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you have to prove that this person is in a certain unit. Actually, we are open -- we have an open mind to all those questions and answers. If you could prove your case, we'll take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this cross-examination has already been watered down with various interjections. But we were talking about the spirit of the language. And I tried to explain what in the spirit of the Croatian language the registration means. So he was registered. He was registered with the Light Assault Military Police Brigade. And now our excellent interpreters are here to tell us how this should be fully interpreted, and it is impossible to do here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I must object again. I'm not sure that Mr. Krsnik is a great expert in the Croatian language, even though he's a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I am not, Your Honours, but I have been speaking it for 45 years, and I know what it means if you say "you're registered." You need not be a great expert in any language, Croatian, Russian, English, or any other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, as I said to you just now, if you have a case, you have the responsibility to prove it. We are not debating on the language issues at this moment. I believe there are some language experts in this Tribunal. Later on, they will verify the exact meaning of the "registration." You may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one comment. I'm not asserting anything. This certificate is asserting it, and the rest is really a matter of the language, into which I don't want to go. But if we need to have an expert on that too, I'm prepared to bring him. But I don't know how many witnesses I'll end up with. However, I'm going to move on. And I thank you for all your comments. Are we in the private session? I'm sorry, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. We're in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask for the private session for a moment again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, during the break, I talked with my colleagues. I wanted to be as effective as possible. And my colleagues told me that perhaps my answer to Judge Clark's question was misinterpreted. The question was: What was my opinion regarding the Benko Penavic ATG and the 4th Battalion, isn't it? And I should like to clarify whether the position of the Defence is that the ATG was within the 4th Battalion. The Defence's position is that on that line, between the intersection and the church, the ATG and the 4th Battalion were together at that time, but otherwise that they were both under the Mostar Defence command. So that is my precise answer to that question regarding the Defence's position. Whether they were under the direct command of the 4th Battalion or not, that, I cannot know. But what is important for me is that all the units on that Bulevar were under the command of the city defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So you are changing your position, Mr. Krsnik. You said quite unequivocally to me that your position was that the ATG was not an independent unit and was part of the 4th Battalion. You're resiling from that position now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not know whether there is anything to resign, because my opinion is that no unit is independent. There is always some command above it. But whether they were an integral part of the 4th Battalion, I said roughly, because of course I cannot say yes or no. But there is absolutely no doubt that they were under the command of the city command. Now, what was between Benko Penavic and the city command, I do not know. Whether it was through the 4th Battalion or whether they were directly under the command of the city defence, we shall endeavour to show it when we take over -- when our case begins. I simply wanted not to be misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I don't think I misinterpreted you, but I accept that you are now saying something a little different from what you said before. But we can go on with the case. I accept what you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, thank you very much for your explanation. And what I want to say is that anyway we have to finish the testimony of this witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yeah, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we have been advised that we can only sit until 1.45, which is a very limited time. Yes, Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness. Well, Mr. Krsnik, you promised us to furnish us with the previous statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not intend -- or rather, I never intended to ask any questions based on this previous statement. I photocopied only this one passage. And here it is. I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the ELMO can be brought down, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sure that you must be tired already, so let's try and focus and bring this examination gradually to its end. I'll try to make my questions as brief as possible, and will you please try to answer as briefly as possible, always about what you know. We were talking about the Oasis restaurant. Do you know how many storeys, how many floors this building has?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or to make precise, ground floor and one storey; is that it, one storey more?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the upper floor where was the billiards, the pool, and downstairs was the restaurant; is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, who was the first one who told you that a conflict would break out at that time? I think it was the 8th of May, if I'm right, when you had this conversation. Was it Mr. Sadzak or Mr. Milicivic who told you that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was Mario Milicivic, Baja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sadzak disarm you, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, were you present throughout the -- were you all together during that meeting, or were you perhaps on the upper floor and Sadzak and Baja on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could anyone frequent that restaurant?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't own it, so I cannot answer your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, you didn't have to be somebody special to be admitted into that restaurant, to be given access?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've just said, I didn't own that restaurant, so that I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we go into private session for a question or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, in 1993, yesterday you mentioned some ethnic cleansings or cleansing. Did you really call it that, that year, 1993?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I called it that, Baja called it that, and all the soldiers in the ATG Benko Penavic unit called it that, and we still call it that way because that is -- like you take a broom and you just sweep it. And we were told to do that, and we swept them by doing what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were a Muslim and still you took part in that?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part in that. As a Muslim, I was forced to take part in that. I had no other option. My biggest -- my principal thoughts at the time were how to get out of it alive, how to save the lives of my parents and other members of my family, so that I was really ready to do anything to save my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did your family leave Mostar? Don't give us the names or anything, just tell us when is it that they left Mostar?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in June? In July? In August? In September? Well, I'm sure you can remember that. I'm not asking you for the date. I'm asking you for a month or an approximate time.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really sorry, but I cannot give you even approximately even the month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So nothing around it. Are your parents where you are at present?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd rather not answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they the first ones to leave?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we have to go into private session briefly. I'd really rather not risk it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in 1992/1993, were you given to drinking or taking drugs?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to go into the private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Question, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The name should be redacted about his relative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go back to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
